subject: EngageAI PoC — post-demo recommended model shortlist and eval pack
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@engageai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: EngageAI PoC recap + recommended shortlist and eval pack

Hi Sara / Maya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — appreciate you walking us through the ingestion flow and sample user journeys. Quick recap and our recommended path forward for the PoC so your team can pick priorities: 

Summary of what matters to you (per call):
- Latency target: p95 generation <= 150ms in the <100 token case for conversational assistant flows
- Cost target: target incremental token cost that keeps demo economics reasonable for pilot users (~$0.03 per 1k tokens or lower if possible)
- Quality: minimize hallucination on factual lookups; maintain helpfulness and instruction-following for prompt templates

Recommended model shortlist (tradeoffs — cost / latency / quality):
1) Redwood-curated-7B-q4f16
   - Rationale: quantized 7B variant, best-in-class inference latency on our Dedicated pools; low cost, excellent instruction-following for short contexts.
   - Expected perf: p95 ~80–120ms (single-request, no batching), token cost: low.
   - Risk: slightly weaker on long multi-step reasoning and rare entity recall.

2) Llama3-13B-fp16 (trimmed KV cache)
   - Rationale: stronger out-of-the-box factuality and nuanced instructions; moderate cost and latency.
   - Expected perf: p95 ~180–260ms, token cost: medium.
   - Risk: may need prompt engineering to hit hallucination targets.

3) Open-70B-int8 (fallback for high-quality risky queries)
   - Rationale: best quality for edge cases and complex reasoning. We propose routing heavier queries to this model as a fallback.
   - Expected perf: p95 >300ms on standard infra; significantly higher cost.
   - Risk: higher cost and latency — keep behind routing policy so only a small fraction of tokens use it.

Deliverables attached: "engageai_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl" (seed prompts + safety filters), "poc_model_shortlist_cost_latency.xlsx" (cost & latency estimations), and "open_eval_summary.pdf" (sanity-check evals vs your sample prompts). Also shared HubSpot link and Drive folder in the metadata.

Immediate next steps we recommend:
- Confirm which metric matters most for the pilot (latency vs cost vs top-1 accuracy) — helps pick single default model
- Accept shortlist and let us run a small-infra benchmark against your sample dataset (we'll need 500–2k sample prompts from your flows)
- Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive next week to align routing, tokenization, and any compliance concerns

Proposed timeline:
- This week: you share 500 sample prompts + priority metric
- Next week: bench run + results review (we'll send perf + cost projections)

Let me know if you want us to prioritize lower-latency baseline or higher-quality baseline — we can provide configuration scripts for both.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

---

From: Sara Nguyen <sara@engageai.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya@engageai.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EngageAI PoC recap + recommended shortlist and eval pack

Thanks Kimberly — that summary is super helpful.

Quick reactions from our side:
- Priority metric: minimize hallucination for factual Q&A, but we still need p95 <= 200ms for most chat flows. So quality first, latency second.
- Of the shortlist we like the Llama3-13B-fp16 as the default, with the Redwood-curated-7B-q4f16 as a lower-cost option for low-risk flows. We want the 70B fallback only for very specific enterprise queries.

Two asks before we lock the PoC config:
1) Can you give an estimated incremental spend for a 10k-query/week pilot for each model?
2) We noticed in the demo that some legal entity names produced confident but incorrect answers — can you include regression checks for hallucinations in the eval pack?

We'll aim to send 600 prompts (mixed user/system) by EOD Friday. If you can run the bench early next week, great.

Best —
Sara Nguyen
Product Manager, EngageAI
sara@engageai.com

On Thu, May 27, 2027 at 02:05 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@engageai.com>, Maya Patel <maya@engageai.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EngageAI PoC recap + recommended shortlist and eval pack

Hi Sara — looping in a few data points and attachments that should answer the spend + regression questions. Attachments: poc_model_shortlist_cost_latency.xlsx (tabbed by model and assumed qps), open_eval_summary.pdf (hallucination/regression checklist), and the prompt pack.

Answers at a glance:
- Estimated incremental spend for 10k queries/week (assume average 50 tokens per response):
  * Redwood-curated-7B-q4f16: ~$95/week (lowest)
  * Llama3-13B-fp16: ~$240/week (middle)
  * Open-70B-int8 (fallback): ~$1,100/week (use sparingly)

- Hallucination/regression checks included: we ran the 300-case legal-entity set you flagged plus an additional 400-case knowledge-check set. Results and false-positive/false-negative rates are summarized in open_eval_summary.pdf. Early takeaway: Llama3-13B-fp16 reduces confident hallucinations by ~18% vs the 7B quantized baseline on this sample.

Operational notes / config suggestions:
- Routing policy: set Llama3-13B-fp16 as default; route to Redwood-curated-7B-q4f16 for non-sensitive flows (based on intent classifier) and only escalate to Open-70B-int8 for >0.85 confidence-scoring failure cases.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for common boilerplate prompts — we estimate 12–18% token reduction on your sample traces.
- Prompt set: see attached "engageai_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl" — includes guarded templates (safety filters), negative examples, and a quick eval harness to reproduce our metrics.

Let us know if you want cost curves for different qps or a version of the spreadsheet with your precise token length distribution — we can plug that in quickly.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara@engageai.com>, Maya Patel <maya@engageai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EngageAI PoC recap + recommended shortlist and eval pack

Great — thanks for the quick turnaround, Ben, and thanks Sara for the clarity on priorities. Agreed on Llama3-13B-fp16 default + 7B quantized as low-cost path + 70B as fallback routing.

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- EngageAI (Sara/Maya): share the 600 sample prompts by EOD Friday (owner: Sara) — include a short label per prompt indicating sensitivity level (public/internal/confidential).
- Redwood (Ben): run benchmark suite against the three model configs and return a short results doc by Tue 31 May. Attach perf + cost projections.
- Redwood (Kimberly): prepare a draft routing policy and minimal eval checklist for hallucination regression tests by Tue 31 May.

I'll schedule the 60-min tech deep-dive for Wed 1 Jun 10:00 AM PT — invite to follow. If that time doesn't work for your team, propose alternatives.

One final ask from our security/compliance pre-check: can you confirm whether any prompts in the sample contain PII or regulated data? That will change the Private deployment checklist.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the bench results.

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
